```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, cache=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.height = 5, fig.width = 10,  fig.cap= ""}
############################################################
# 3 scenarios of plant–pollinator networks
# with different Apis dominance
# + network plots (Poll1 & Poll2 coloured, Apis black)
# + single summary barplot (Degree, Morisita, PDI)
############################################################

############################################################
# 3 scenarios of plant–pollinator networks
# with different Apis dominance
############################################################

## Load libraries ----
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(data.table)
library(patchwork)
library(tidyr)
library(grid)

source("../Scripts/compute_metric_function.R")

# LOW dominance --------------------------------------------
# High overlap with Apis + high specialisation
M_low <- matrix(
  c(3,   2.5, 0,
    3,   0,   2.5,
    0,   2,   0,
    0,   0,   2),
  nrow = 4,
  byrow = TRUE
)

# MEDIUM dominance -----------------------------------------
# Broader diets, partial shift, moderate overlap
M_med <- matrix(
  c(5,   1.5, 0.5,
    5,   0.5, 1.5,
    2,   1.5, 1.5,
    0.5, 1.5, 1.5),
  nrow = 4,
  byrow = TRUE
)

# HIGH dominance -------------------------------------------
# Apis dominates core plants; others generalise but shift away
M_high <- matrix(
  c(8,   0.2, 0.1,
    7,   0.3, 0.2,
    1,   1.5, 1.5,
    0.5, 1.5, 1.5),
  nrow = 4,
  byrow = TRUE
)

set_dimnames <- function(M) {
  colnames(M) <- c("Apis", "Poll1", "Poll2")
  rownames(M) <- c("Plant1", "Plant2", "Plant3", "Plant4")
  M
}

M_low  <- set_dimnames(M_low)
M_med  <- set_dimnames(M_med)
M_high <- set_dimnames(M_high)

############################################################
## Helper: build network plot + metrics -------------------
############################################################

build_scenario <- function(M, title) {
  # Edge list
  edges <- as.data.frame(as.table(M)) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      Plant      = Var1,
      Pollinator = Var2,
      Weight     = Freq
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Weight > 0)
  
  # Node coordinates
  plants <- data.frame(
    name = rownames(M),
    x    = 0,
    y    = seq(1, nrow(M))
  )
  
  polls <- data.frame(
    name = colnames(M),
    x    = 1,
    y    = seq(1.5, 3.5, length.out = ncol(M))
  )
  
  # ---- node strength (total interactions per species) ----
  plant_strength <- rowSums(M)          # sum over pollinators
  poll_strength  <- colSums(M)          # sum over plants
  
  plants$strength <- plant_strength[plants$name]
  polls$strength  <- poll_strength[polls$name]
  
  nodes <- rbind(plants, polls)
  
  # Edges + coordinates
  edges_xy <- edges %>%
    dplyr::left_join(nodes, by = c("Plant" = "name")) %>%
    dplyr::rename(x1 = x, y1 = y) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(nodes, by = c("Pollinator" = "name")) %>%
    dplyr::rename(x2 = x, y2 = y)
  
  # Colour groups
  edges_xy <- edges_xy %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Pollinators = dplyr::case_when(
        Pollinator == "Poll1" ~ "Species 1",
        Pollinator == "Poll2" ~ "Species 2",
        TRUE                  ~ "Honeybee"
      )
    )
  
  polls <- polls %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Pollinators = dplyr::case_when(
        name == "Poll1" ~ "Species 1",
        name == "Poll2" ~ "Species 2",
        TRUE            ~ "Honeybee"
      )
    )
  
  # Long format for metrics
  df_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(M)) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      plant       = Var1,
      pollinator  = Var2,
      interaction = Freq
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(interaction > 0)
  
  metrics <- compute_metrics(
    df              = df_long,
    focal_species   = "Apis",
    return_observed = TRUE
  )
  
  # ---- NETWORK plot ----
  p_net <- ggplot() +
    # edges: linewidth ∝ interaction strength
    geom_segment(
      data = edges_xy,
      aes(x = x1, y = y1,
          xend = x2, yend = y2,
          linewidth = Weight,
          color = Pollinators),
      alpha = 0.4,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
      "Species 1" = viridis::viridis(3)[1],
      "Species 2" = viridis::viridis(3)[2],
      "Honeybee"  = "orange2"
    )) +
    scale_linewidth(range = c(0.3, 2)) +
    
    # plant species: point size ∝ total interactions
geom_point(
  data = plants,
  aes(x = x, y = y, size = strength, shape = "Plants"),
  color = "gray53",
  fill  = "gray53",
  stroke = 1
) +
    scale_shape_manual(
  name = "Plant species",
  values = c("Plants" = 22),
  label="")+
    geom_point(
      data = polls,
      aes(x = x, y = y, size = strength, color = Pollinators)
    ) +
    
    scale_size(range = c(3, 8)) +
guides(
  linewidth = "none",
  size = "none",
  colour = guide_legend(order = 1, 
    override.aes = list(       
      size = 6,        # big legend points
      alpha = 1,       # full opacity for legend
      stroke = 1,      # clear outline
      linewidth = 0    # <-- removes the line in the legend
    )
  ),
  shape = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(       
    size = 6,
    color = "gray53",
    fill  = "gray53",
    shape = 22
  ))) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.margin  = margin(5, 20, 5, 20),
      panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", 
                                  fill = NA, linewidth = 0.6),
      plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
    ) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.2)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.2)) +
    ggtitle(title)+
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)) +
    theme(
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    legend.title       = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.key.size    = unit(1, "cm")
  )
  
  list(plot = p_net, metrics = metrics)
}

############################################################
## 3. Build scenarios & combine with arrow ----------------
############################################################

sc_low  <- build_scenario(M_low,  "Low")
sc_med  <- build_scenario(M_med,  "Medium")
sc_high <- build_scenario(M_high, "High")

networks_row <- sc_low$plot | sc_med$plot | sc_high$plot


## TOP TRIANGLE ----
df_tri_top <- data.frame(
  x = c(1, 0, 1),
  y = c(-1.2, -0.7, -0.2)
)

triangle_top <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data  = df_tri_top,
    aes(x, y),
    fill  = alpha("black", 0.2),
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(-0.5, 1.2), clip = "off") +
  theme_void() +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.5, y = 0.1,
    label = "Honeybee dominance",
    fontface = "bold", size = 5.5
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")  # just to be explicit


## BOTTOM TRIANGLE ----
df_tri_bottom <- data.frame(
  x = c(0, 1, 0),
  y = c(-0.6, -0.3, 0.4)
)

triangle_bottom <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data  = df_tri_bottom,
    aes(x, y),
    fill  = alpha("black", 0.2),
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.5, y = 0.6,
    label = "Resource overlap and specialisation",
    fontface = "bold", size = 5.5
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(0, 1),
    # ↑ Increase the upper limit to create empty space on TOP,
    #    which visually pushes the triangle DOWN in the panel:
    ylim = c(-0.2, 1.4),
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    # a bit of panel margin so it doesn't hug the legend
    plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 5, b = 0, l = 5)
  )

## FINAL UNIFIED PLOT ----
final_plot <- triangle_top / networks_row / triangle_bottom +
  plot_layout(
    # make the bottom row a bit shorter so the legend sits closer up
    heights = c(1.25, 6, 1.25),
    guides  = "collect"
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    # negative top margin pulls the legend upward
    legend.margin = margin(t = -70, b = 5),
        plot.margin = margin(t = -5, r = 0, b = 20, l = 0)

  )

final_plot
```
